For Black Friday, Amazon is offering the lowest price I've seen on ASUS' powerful ultraportable gaming convertible. You can pick up a brand new Asus ROG Flow Z13 gaming laptop with 32GB of RAM for just $1,699.99 with free shipping after a $400 off discount. The Asus Flow Z13 (in tablet mode) isn't much bigger or heavier than a handheld gaming PC, but it boasts way better gaming performance that rivals full-sized laptops.

The Asus ROG Flow Z13 Gaming Laptop Drops Below $2,000

The Asus ROG Flow Z13 is a 13.4" 2-in-1 convertible laptop that weighs in at only 2.65 pounds without the detachable keyboard. That's about one pound heavier than the Xbox Ally X handheld, which weighs in at 1.6 pounds. With the keyboard, the Z13 weighs about 3.5 pounds. A premium laptop deserves premium build quality, and the Flow Z13 doesn't disappoint with a blacked out CNC aluminum alloy chassis and Corning Gorilla Glass Victus screen protection.

This particular configuration is equipped with a 13.4" 2560x1600 180Hz IPS display, AMD Ryzen AI Max 390 CPU with AMD Radeon 8050S iGPU, 32GB of LPDDR5X-8000Mhz RAM, and a 1TB SSD. This is less powerful than the highest end ROG Flow Z13, which comes equipped with a Ryzen AI Max 395 CPU with 8060S iGPU, but it's also far less expensive (currently the least expensive model is $2,100 ). The Radeon 8050S is more powerful than the Ryzen Z2 Extreme APU found in the highest-end handheld gaming PCs like the ROG Xbox Ally X.

Asus ROG Flow Z13 Review by Chris Coke

The Asus ROG Flow Z13 is a fantastic 2-in-1 laptop-tablet for a particular kind of user, those who want that versatility with the best performance possible for productivity and gaming in this form factor – talk about multifaceted. It’s an exciting glimpse at what laptops may offer in the future, too.

Upgrade to the Ryzen AI Max 395+ model for $1,980

If you're looking to maximize your laptop's gaming capabilities within the ultra-portable form factor, then this Z13 Flow upgrade would actually be worth the $280 premium. The AMD Ryzen AI Max 395+ boasts 16 CPU cores compared to the 12 cores on the 390 as well as a 100MHz speed bump. Neither of these will noticeably improve gaming performance. Instead, the reason to upgrade would be for the iGPU; the Max 395+ replaces the Radeon 8050S found in the 390 to the more powerful Radeon 8060S, which equates to about 10%-15% more frames in games.
